measured_RAM_config: 4 channels DDR4-2133; 12 workers sequential 4GiB read, warmed5 repeats
limits: DRAM counters unavailable by user choice; no measured physical DRAM traffic or measured 4-vs8channel inference comparison.
Channel table is a sensitivity calculation, not a forecast. Memory service fraction10/25/40% is assumed, not measured.
Equal channel efficiency and DDR4-2666 operation are assumed; CPU model, DIMM ranks and platform can change them.
Logical CPU weight traffic counts expert token-rows; multi-token kernels may reuse weights, so it is not an actual DRAM byte count.
Three times staging payload approximates one source read, one destination write and one DMA read; cache behavior can change physical DRAM bytes.
These proxies omit activation/Engram/control traffic and HIP copy details; they are neither total traffic nor rigorous bounds.
Do not multiply CPU, PCIe and RAM what-if gains; work overlaps and the bottleneck changes.
interpretation: At35tok/s the logical-weight+3xstaging planning proxy is below current58.9GB/s sequential read ceiling. This does not establish bandwidth sufficiency under contention, but there is no evidence that eight channels are required to reach35. Additional compute/PCIe capacity remains a plausible benefit.
